TETCN Final Overview

TETCN final experiments

The architecture of every model in the final Pareto experiments, with its tuning results at each parameter budget. Pick a dataset, context and arm, and show either the architecture diagrams or the learning-rate search charts (mean validation F1 against learning rate, each chart from 0.1 below its lowest mean to 1.00, best rate ringed). Each card shows one model at one budget and, below, its best tuned result so far (test F1 at the best learning rate, mean ± SD over 15 fits: 5 random-window splits × 3 seeds).

F1 is the balanced macro F1 used to pick rates (classes weighted equally; on CC25 captures within a class too). Updated 2026-11-21 17:11 UTC.

  • Depth by repetitionThe whole stage chain repeats 1, 2, 5, 10 times at 10K, 100K, 1M, 10M. Each repeat has its own weights.
  • One shared widthAll stages of a model use one width, solved so the parameter count lands on the budget.
  • 3 GDN layers per TE layerIn the GDN hybrid a repeat holds 9 GDN layers, 3 Transformer layers and 4 TCN blocks, with skips around the Transformer and TCN stages.
  • 3 attention layers, 1 attention residualEvery Transformer stage is 3 attention layers followed by one attention residual: the state becomes a learned softmax mix of the projected input and the states after each earlier group of 3.
  • Size encodingPacket size (CC25: flow bytes and bytes per packet) also enters as sin and cos of its value at 4 frequencies, in every model except the base TCN.
  • Causal versionsAdded Nov 20: cTE, cTETCN and GDNcTETCN, the Transformer models made causal so they can classify a flow packet by packet. Same layers and parameter counts; what differs is set out in “Causal and non-causal Transformer” below.
  • With XGBoostA smaller network (75% of the budget) feeds its pooled vector (causal models: the last step's state) plus the raw inputs to XGBoost, whose tree nodes take the other 25%. Not run at 10K on TLS and QUIC: one boosting round there is already 1,575 to 2,700 tree nodes.

Causal and non-causal Transformer

The causal models differ from TE, TETCN and GDNTETCN only in how the Transformer sees the sequence and in how the model is read out and trained. Layers, widths and parameter counts are the same.

Non-causal: TE, TETCN, GDNTETCNCausal: cTE, cTETCN, GDNcTETCN
AttentionEvery step attends to every step of the window.Causal mask: step t attends to steps 1 to t only.
PositionSinusoidal positional encoding added before the Transformer layers.None (NoPE): order comes from the mask, and from the GDN and TCN stages.
ReadoutMean of the final hidden states over all steps, then the classifier.The classifier at every step; the window’s answer is the last step’s prediction.
LossOne cross-entropy per window.Cross-entropy at every step against the window’s label, weighted by a softsign of the step’s position: u = t/L, x = 2u − 1, w = x/(1 + |x|) + ½ (0 to 1 over the window), normalised over the window, so later steps count more.
ReportedTest F1 of the window’s answer.The same, plus test F1 after every step: AUC (mean over the steps) and the first, middle and last thirds.
Learning rateTuned per setting.Tuned per setting, starting at the same-size TE’s best.
  • The same in both3 attention layers per Transformer stage, then one attention residual; width, heads, feed-forward size and dropout; the packet-size sin and cos features; the input projection; one linear classifier; the parameter budgets. The mask and the sinusoidal encoding have no weights, so the parameter counts are identical.
  • Attention residualIt mixes a step’s states across depth, never across steps, so it stays causal unchanged.
  • HybridscTETCN and GDNcTETCN change only the Transformer stage (mask, no positions) and use the per-step readout and loss. The GDN and TCN stages and the skips work step by step already, so the whole chain can run one packet at a time.
  • Padding (TLS, QUIC)Flows shorter than the context are zero-padded at the end, and neither model masks padding in attention. The non-causal mean includes the padded steps; the causal model’s last step comes after the flow ended and has seen every real packet. In training those steps keep the flow’s label and carry softsign’s full weight.
